entries.name: 기존 시점 · 왼쪽 조준
entries.prompt:
Precise concept-image edit, camera continuity is the highest priority. IMAGE1 is the USER-APPROVED indoor gameplay view and is the BASE IMAGE to preserve. IMAGE2 is the approved highway gameplay camera/framing reference. Keep Image1's camera, perspective, floor projection, room, wall/ceiling geometry, NPC distances and apparent scales UNCHANGED. Do not zoom out, pull the camera back, raise/lower it, orbit it, reframe the scene or expose extra floor at the bottom. This is the same game camera after entering the restaurant.
HARD SCREEN COMPOSITION: the player must remain the dominant near-foreground SHARK at the BOTTOM CENTER, as in both approved references. Keep the shark's fixed ground pivot around x=50%, y=82% of the full image; its complete body belongs in the LOWER THIRD (roughly y=66%–94%), NOT at mid-height. The player must be as close/large as the original shark, with rotation changing its silhouette naturally. The middle/top are the police and environment ahead. No large policeman back/shoulder in the foreground, no observer standing between camera and player. The camera is attached to the original gameplay viewing location, NOT to a policeman and NOT an arena spectator camera.
GAMEPLAY:30-second stationary holdout; world position remains fixed, only the shark BODY/aim rotates relative to this fixed camera. Exactly ONE shark, no ghost duplicates. Behind-camera/off-screen police remain OFF SCREEN. Do not try to fit every attacker or every door into this picture. No top-down, bird's-eye, wide arena, cutaway or stage overview.
Change ONLY the player's yaw/pose, the aim direction of its existing blue water shots and the small concept label. Preserve the approved restaurant's clear fight space, three-head-tall HUMAN police (no animals), blue/cream/timber counters, red vending, warm lights and ceiling. No bonus pedestals. Keep the original compact30-second UI area; replace its text with "30초 · 회전 방어" and "위치 고정". Do not add a huge rotation circle, visible arena platform or empty dance floor under the shark; at most one subtle short curved arrow close to a sneaker to clarify turning.
SHARK identity: gray-blue horizontal animal body, dorsal fin and white underside. Exactly two short leg supports in one left/right pair with two cyan-white sneakers, one long tail ending directly in a third sneaker. No extra pair of legs, no humanoid shark torso, no handheld gun. Body changes orientation coherently while staying planted at the original bottom-center floor position. Single directional water shot from the SNOUT, never from its back or tail.
POSE D1: rotate the shark in place about60–80degrees toward SCREEN LEFT. We see its leftward side/three-quarter-back profile in the BOTTOM THIRD, with head toward left and tail extending right. Keep its center of mass/pivot low at82% image height; do not move it up to the room's center to fit the side silhouette. A short blue water shot leaves the snout diagonally LEFT toward a police officer at the existing left midground, who remains ahead of the player; original other human police ahead can remain. Do not bring any policeman closer to camera than the shark. Small top-left label exactly "D1 · 기존 시점 / 왼쪽 조준".
